definitions.explanation: A divine being worshipped in religion.
A sacred spirit in Shinto belief.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{神|かみ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{祈|いの}った→祈る：01198_inoru⟧。
examples.english: I prayed to the gods at the shrine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{神様|かみさま}→神様：00161_kamisama⟧、⟦どうか→どうか：09854_douka⟧⟦お{守|まも}りください→守る：01986_mamoru⟧。
⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{八百万|やおよろず}→八百万：11990_yaoyorozu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{神|かみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: In Japan, there are eight million gods.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自然|しぜん}→自然：01423_shizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦あらゆる→あらゆる：03824_arayuru⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{神|かみ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{宿|やど}る→宿る：12351_yadoru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{信|しん}じられている→信じる：01111_shinjiru⟧。
examples.english: It is believed that spirits dwell in all things in nature.

notes:
{神|かみ} means god, deity, or spirit. In Japanese culture, this concept differs significantly from Western monotheism.

SHINTO CONCEPT:
In Shinto, {神|かみ} (⟦{八百万|やおよろず}→八百万：11990_yaoyorozu⟧の{神|かみ} = 'eight million gods') refers to spirits inhabiting nature, ancestors, and sacred places. Almost anything can be considered a {神|かみ}.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{神様|かみさま}→神様：00161_kamisama⟧: god (honorific form)
- ⟦{神社|じんじゃ}→神社：01620_jinja⟧: Shinto shrine
- ⟦{神道|しんとう}→神道：09586_shintou⟧: Shinto
- ⟦{神話|しんわ}→神話：00367_shinwa⟧: mythology
- ⟦{神棚|かみだな}→神棚：13740_kamidana⟧: household Shinto altar

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {神|かみ}に⟦{祈|いの}る→祈る：01198_inoru⟧: to pray to god(s)
- ⟦{神頼|かみだの}み→神頼み：15476_kamidanomi⟧: relying on divine help
- ⟦{神|かみ}{業|わざ}→神業：27806_kamiwaza⟧: divine work, miraculous skill

MODERN SLANG:
{神|かみ} is used colloquially to mean 'amazing' or 'godlike': この⟦{曲|きょく}→曲：09881_kyoku⟧{神|かみ}! (This song is amazing!)
